definition: a loan taken to buy property, secured against that same property
hook: Every mortgage you sign is, in the oldest sense, a pledge unto death.
modernAnchor: A mortgage is a home loan to us. Thirty years, monthly payments, the bank holding the deed.
journey: The word comes from Old French: mort, meaning dead, and gage, meaning a pledge or security.
A medieval jurist explained the grim name two ways, and both of them end in death.
If the debtor failed to pay, the pledged land was lost to him forever, dead to his hands.
And if he paid in full, the pledge itself died, released and dissolved. Dead either way.
